_doc: The Grand Staircase's moving flights (sim_core::stairs; docs/architecture.md). Each flight is two stair surfaces of data/world/layout.json tagged moving {flight, position}: `a` (its resting place in the layout) and `b`, which is `a` turned by `angle_deg` about the vertical axis through `pivot` [x, z] (right-handed, y up: a point (dx, dz) from the pivot goes to (dx cos a + dz sin a, -dx sin a + dz cos a)). The schedule is a pure function of the server's clock, the same on every end, with no message: a flight switches position every `period_s` seconds at epoch_ms + (phase + k) x period (k even: to A, odd: to B); the `swing_s` seconds before a switch it swings toward its next position, the `warning_s` before that it shudders (the chat line, dust). Moves within `grace_ms` of a switch are accepted against the old or the new position. `dev_period_s` is the short period a development server, the load test and a client may all opt into together (never in production). Each gate is a short railing gate on a landing edge a flight meets: open while its flight rests in `position`, closing over `gate_s` as the flight swings away, opening over `gate_s` after it arrives; `line` is the gate's two hinges [x, z] (two leaves, one from each hinge), `opens` the unit direction [dx, dz] the leaves swing to (onto the landing). Flights are in the layout's order: bit i of a staircase state is flights[i] at B.
